statement: One line holds m and n. You stand on the top-left cell of an m by n grid and may move only right or down; print the number of distinct paths to the bottom-right cell. State: f(i, j) is the number of paths into cell (i, j). Transition: a path arrives from above or from the left, so f(i, j) = f(i-1, j) + f(i, j-1), with the first row and column all 1. One row of the table suffices as rolling storage.
constraints: The answer fits in a 64-bit integer.

example.why: Every path mixes 2 downs with 6 rights; choosing where the downs go gives 28 arrangements.

hint: Roll a single row left to right: each cell adds the cell above (its old value) to the cell left of it.
mistake: Counting diagonal moves or revisits - only right and down exist, so paths can no more loop than go back.
